stability: Every entry in `outputs` is stable API: labels, basenames, and the field names/nesting shown in each example. Removing or renaming any of them is a breaking change and requires a TOOL_VERSION bump plus a changelog note here. Files NOT listed here (per-chunk intermediates under segment_chunks/, the resampled/ conversion intermediate) are internal and may change or vanish without notice. `description` is one line by design — it is joined verbatim into each get_job_status outputs[] entry as `desc`.

speech.description: Speech-only stem WAV (Bandit v2; 16 kHz mono default, configurable) — listening/reference product (review lanes, voice ID); not recommended as an ASR/diarization input today (the original mix measured better and is the validated default); absent when speech_stem=false

contents.format: RIFF/WAVE, 16-bit PCM, mono, one data chunk — full source duration, chunks already concatenated

speech.notes: Bandit v2 separated speech stem (dialogue, voiceover, commentary). The 16 kHz default suits reference-audio consumers and ASR engines alike. Measured on the CURRENT model: the stem deletes low-prominence speech outright and lost to the original mix on word error rate — so the mix is the validated transcription/diarization input and feeding the stem instead is not recommended today; if you do, compare against a mix-based transcript. The model will improve and this will be re-measured. rms_db/duration_sec for QC live in the metrics file's stem_summary.speech.

music.description: Music-only stem WAV (Bandit v2; 48 kHz mono default, configurable) — use for music ID, audio timeline lanes, remixing; absent when music_stem=false

contents.format: RIFF/WAVE, 16-bit PCM, mono, one data chunk — full source duration, chunks already concatenated

music.notes: Bandit v2 separated music stem (score, theme music, jingles). The 48 kHz default preserves full fidelity for remixing and music identification. rms_db/duration_sec for QC live in the metrics file's stem_summary.music.

sfx.description: SFX/ambience stem WAV (Bandit v2; 32 kHz mono default, configurable) — use for effects lanes, remixing, audio activity detection; absent when sfx_stem=false

contents.format: RIFF/WAVE, 16-bit PCM, mono, one data chunk — full source duration, chunks already concatenated

sfx.notes: Bandit v2 separated effects stem (sound effects, ambience, foley). rms_db/duration_sec for QC live in the metrics file's stem_summary.sfx.

speech-safe.description: Gated-mix speech WAV (opt-in via speech_safe=true; 48 kHz mono default): the speech stem with attenuated ORIGINAL mix patched into the spans the separator deleted (quiet/background speech), crossfaded — guaranteed never silent where the source had sound. Use it wherever the track is played or mixed: audio-description mixes, review/QC playback, dialogue-forward renders. As an ASR input the original mix measured better pooled and is the validated default, while music-heavy episodes measured ahead on speech_safe — compare per content class

contents.format: RIFF/WAVE, 16-bit PCM, mono, one data chunk — full source duration, chunks already concatenated

speech-safe.notes: The separation model deletes low-prominence speech outright (whispers, phone voices, background talkers — a property of its training data; no inference knob recovers it). Inside each deleted span this file carries attenuated original mix (speech plus reduced background) instead of silence; everywhere else it is the raw speech stem unchanged. Patched spans are therefore MIX-flavored, not separated — the per-run gap evidence is stem_activity.json's speech_stem_gaps lane, and per-chunk patch spans with the gate parameters live in each segment_chunks/chunk_NNN.json. audio_speech.wav is unaffected and still produced per speech_stem. As an ASR input (measured, 27-ep caption corpus): the original mix is the validated default (11.08% vs speech_safe 12.22% pooled WER); speech_safe measured AHEAD of the mix on music-heavy/uncaptioned-heavy episodes (it suppresses sung-lyric hallucinations) and recovered 3,669 stem-deleted words vs the bare stem — if you feed it to ASR, compare against a mix transcript for your content class first.

metrics.description: Aggregate separation metrics (per-stem summary, timings, per-chunk summaries) — use for QC via rms_db/duration_sec and locating stem WAVs via output_keys; keys track the stems actually produced
metrics.notes: output_keys, stem_summary, and each chunks[].stems dict are keyed per ACTIVE stem and carry an entry for every name in stems_produced — the example shows one; speech_safe appears as its own name there when requested. chunks[].timing_ms `{stem}_decoder` keys track the decoders that RAN — speech_safe=true runs the speech decoder even when speech_stem=false, so speech_decoder can appear without a speech entry in stems_produced. audio_key is the 48 kHz mono WAV the model actually consumed: the source itself on the WAV fast path, resampled/audio_48k_mono.wav (internal) or the wav under media-processing's own run prefix when conversion ran. timing_ms.total_wall is the slowest chunk (Map runs in parallel); total_compute is the sum. Each chunks[].metrics_key points at that chunk's own segment_chunks/chunk_NNN.json — an internal file, not contract.

stem-activity.description: Semantic audio timelines: per-lane activity spans (original = non-silence of the mix; each active stem = energy above threshold), the speech_stem_gaps lane (mix active while the speech stem is near-silent — audio the stem does not cover; an upper bound on deleted speech, since music/sfx-only passages qualify too), plus line-up tones measured on the original — use for ad-break/dialogue-gap logic, stem-coverage visibility, and bars-and-tone joins; deliberately carries NO bars_and_tone verdict, that is the fusion layer's call; absent (with stem_waveforms) on pre-alpha.20260826a runs and when the analysis pass degraded — stem WAVs are unaffected
stem-activity.notes: speech_stem_gaps is present exactly when speech_stem was enabled — it compares the mix envelope against the RAW speech envelope at absolute dBFS (which only exists here; the waveform JSON is peak-normalized), so speech_safe alone cannot produce it: the patched lane would hide the very gaps it exists to show. A gap means the source wasn't silent but the speech stem is — in dialogue regions that is deletion evidence; in music/sfx-only passages it is correct rejection, so the lane is an UPPER BOUND on deleted speech and naming what a gap MEANS is the fusion layer's job (join with the transcript or diarization). The lane and the speech_safe patch gate are DIFFERENT instruments and neither is a subset of the other: the lane reads the DELIVERED (resampled) stem with a 500 ms bridge and 250 ms minimum span, while the patch gate runs pre-resample with a lower mix floor, a 250 ms bridge, and no minimum span. The authoritative record of what audio_speech_safe.wav patched is each chunk's segment_chunks/chunk_NNN.json patch spans (internal).

stem-waveforms.description: Rendering envelopes: peak-normalized per-bin RMS for the original mix and each active stem at params.bin_ms resolution — use to draw timeline waveform lanes without reading the WAVs; absent on pre-alpha.20260826a runs and when the analysis pass degraded

usage.description: Per-state durations and estimated cost, media-processing child included when conversion ran — use for reporting what this run cost
usage.notes: Costs are us-east-1 arm64 estimates, not billing data. media_processing is null unless the source needed format conversion; when present it is {execution_arn, pipeline_wall_sec, estimated_cost, states} sourced from media-processing's own published usage_tracking.json (its states entries follow THAT stack's usage shape, not this one's), and its estimated_cost is already summed into total_estimated_cost. The final 'Usage tracking' states entry estimates its own duration (its terminal event has not fired when it writes this file) and omits retried/incomplete. retried counts billed failed attempts; incomplete is true only for an attempt with no terminal event in the history.
